summary.text: The asthenosphere is the mechanically weak, ductile part of Earth's upper mantle, lying just below the rigid lithosphere.
It is almost solid, but a slight amount of melting, less than 0.1% of the rock, helps make it weak.
The rigid lithosphere is thought to float and move on this slowly flowing layer, and melting where it wells upward is the most important source of magma on Earth.

facts.label: Top depth
facts.value: About 80 to 200 km below the surface

items.prompt: Seismic waves slow down as they pass from the lithosphere into the layer beneath it. What does that slowdown tell seismologists about the deeper layer?

options.label: It is colder than the rock above
It is less rigid than the rock above
It is completely molten rock
It is made of metal like the core

items.explain: Seismic waves move more slowly through less rigid rock, so the slower speeds revealed a weaker layer below the lithosphere.

items.prompt: S waves cannot travel through liquid, yet they do cross the asthenosphere. What does that show about the layer?

options.label: It is hotter than the outer core
It is mostly water and gas
It is fully liquid but very thick
It cannot be fully melted

items.explain: Because the asthenosphere transmits S waves, it cannot be fully melted, even if it holds a very small share of melt.

items.prompt: Where does the largest share of Earth's magma come from?

options.label: Ocean plates melting as they sink
Liquid iron leaking from the outer core
Rising asthenosphere melting as pressure drops
Friction heat along big faults

items.explain: Decompression melting of asthenosphere rock creeping upward is the most important source of magma on Earth, most of it erupting at mid-ocean ridges.

items.prompt: The same mantle rock sits at two depths: one shallow and cooler, one deeper and hotter. How does it behave in each place?

options.label: Rigid when shallow, flowing slowly when deep
Flowing slowly when shallow, rigid when deep
Rigid at both depths
Liquid at both depths

items.explain: Closer to the surface at lower temperatures the mantle behaves rigidly, while deeper down at higher temperatures it moves in a ductile way.

items.prompt: Tectonic plates are rigid slabs, yet they shift across the globe. What do geologists think lets them move?

options.label: They float on an ocean of liquid magma
They slide on the liquid outer core
They are dragged by ocean currents
They ride on a weak, slowly flowing layer

items.explain: The rigid lithosphere is thought to float or move on the slowly flowing asthenosphere, which is almost solid rather than liquid.

items.prompt: At a mid-ocean ridge, how close to the seafloor does the boundary between the rigid plate and the weak layer below come?

options.label: About 200 kilometres
Within a few kilometres
About 100 kilometres
About 700 kilometres

items.explain: At mid-ocean ridges the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary rises to within a few kilometres of the ocean floor.
